features.roles: A project role that may create revisions (Engineer and above)

features.roles: Issue revisions or Configure documents (Lead engineer and above); versions only for people who see them

features.title: Delete and restore a version or revision

features.summary: E1 proposes where every signal of a group of devices lands, junction box, multicore pair and I/O channel, keeping the segregation rules, redundancy groups and spares, and says why for each choice; you walk the proposal hop by hop in Panorama EI&C, change a junction box for one device or all, and accept a hop, a device or everything.
features.roles: A license and a project role that may edit relationships

features.title: Changes after issue: the wire move list
features.summary: Once wiring is issued for construction, a change is a list for the field: moving a device to another junction box lifts and lands its cores and keeps everything else, and a device to be removed keeps its wiring until the field has lifted it.
features.roles: A license and a project role that may edit relationships

features.title: Entity check and voltage budget
features.summary: For an intrinsically safe loop E1 checks the barrier against the device and the cable for its length (the entity check), and for every loop with a supply the voltage left at the device at 20 mA. A value it needs and does not have is reported as missing.
features.roles: Anyone who may view the project

features.title: Cabinet fill and heat balance
features.summary: On a cabinet's or junction box's page: each strip and card as a bar of what is used, spare and free, and the cabinet's heat balance from physics: its inside and top temperature, the margin to its limit, the cooling missing, and which devices give the most heat.
features.roles: Anyone who may view the project

features.title: Exchange the I/O list with the control-system vendor
features.summary: Export the I/O list of a unit or a cabinet for the control-system vendor, and import their list back: a channel they kept comes back fixed, a channel they changed is a finding, and is moved to when you apply it.
features.roles: Exporting: anyone who may view the project. Importing: a license and a project role that may edit relationships

features.title: Markers and the block diagram
features.summary: Export the wire, terminal and cable markers of a cabinet for the printer's software, and see the block diagram: the locations, the enclosures in them, and the cables between them.
features.roles: Anyone who may view the project

features.title: Fieldbus segments
features.summary: Make a fieldbus segment from a segment typical, place Foundation Fieldbus H1 and Profibus PA devices on its coupler ports within its limits, and see the segment against its limits on its page.
features.roles: A license and a project role that may create objects; anyone who may view the project sees the segment view

features.title: Status sets and the project's statuses
features.summary: Every object, sheet, document and task has a status from a status set: the five categories New, Active, Resolved, Closed and Removed, with sub-statuses a set adds under them. Configuration → Statuses makes a set and chooses the one each level reads.
features.roles: Seeing statuses: everyone who can view the project. Making a project's status set and choosing the sets: Manage project workflows (Project administrator); a company set: Edit the company library

features.title: The status chip: set an item's status
features.summary: Under an object's name the status chip shows its status (its category before it when they differ), HOLD, and No workflow. Click it to set another status of its set.
features.roles: Setting a status: Move items in their workflow (Engineer and above)

features.title: Value statuses: Assumed, Preliminary, Confirmed, Final
features.summary: A value carries a status of its own, set from its row's right-click menu and shown by a mark after its name. A Confirmed or Final value that changes becomes Preliminary again. Calculated values have none.
features.roles: Set value statuses (Engineer and above) and edit attributes

features.title: Put an item or a value on hold
features.summary: Put on hold… with a reason marks an object, a sheet, a document or one value HOLD, with who and why; Release hold takes it off. A hold never blocks editing; it is a filter and a column in the query view.
features.roles: Put on hold (Lead engineer, Project administrator)

features.title: Statuses and holds on the drawing
features.summary: Layers ▸ Status tints each symbol on a 2D space by its status, with a legend at the bottom left; Layers ▸ Show holds marks every held item HOLD. Both are off until you turn them on, for you and that 2D space only.
features.roles: Everyone who can view the project

features.title: Workflows: steps an item moves through
features.summary: A workflow is the statuses of a status set in order, its steps, with a credit, a time limit and a lock each may have. Make one from a template (Engineering deliverable, ISO 19650 deliverable, Instrument data, Diagram, Engineering object) in Configuration → Workflows.
features.roles: Making a project's workflow: Manage project workflows (Project administrator); a company workflow: Edit the company library

features.title: Assign workflows and start them
features.summary: Assignments say which workflow the project's items follow: objects by class (then their parent classes, then any class), sheets, documents, tasks. Apply starts the workflow on every item that has not started it, as one change.
features.roles: Manage project workflows (Project administrator)

features.title: Move an item to another step
features.summary: On the status chip an item with a workflow moves: to the next step, back to an earlier one with a reason, to Removed and back with a reason. A held item does not move forward; in a locked step its values, name and tag wait until it is moved back. In a query view, Move to… moves the selected rows' items at once.
features.roles: Move items in their workflow (Engineer and above)

features.title: The workflow board
features.summary: A workflow's items as cards in a column per step and Removed, with their days in the step, returns and HOLD. Drag a card to another column, or use Move to… on it, to move it.
features.roles: Seeing the board: everyone who can view the project; moving cards: Move items in their workflow

features.title: Exit criteria: what an item needs before it moves on
features.summary: A step may say what an item needs before it moves on: required values filled in, values confirmed and not on hold, related items far enough, no open errors, a revision issued, a checklist ticked, a condition. The status chip lists them with ticks and crosses; an item whose criteria all pass shows Ready to move.
features.roles: Seeing criteria: everyone who can view the project; ticking a checklist: Move items in their workflow

features.title: Approvals: sign or reject a step
features.summary: A step with an approval moves on only by its signatures: each sign-off step (Checked, Approved) is signed by someone who did not move the item into it, or sign an earlier step it names. A rejection with a reason sends the item back. An item changed after its approval shows Changed since Approved.
features.roles: Sign workflow approvals (Engineer and above, Reviewer), with a fresh sign-in

features.title: Override failing criteria
features.summary: With Override workflow checks, Override… moves an item on although a blocking criterion fails, with a reason that is kept with the item's step and in its history. An approval cannot be overridden.
features.roles: Override workflow checks (Lead engineer, Project administrator)

features.title: The flow: paths between steps
features.summary: Flow shows a workflow's steps in order with their credit, lock, criteria and approval, and its paths above them: extra moves such as Skip check (small change), each with an optional condition on the item. Add path… adds one and publishes a new version.
features.roles: Manage project workflows (Project administrator)

features.title: New workflow versions in a project
features.summary: A new version of a workflow reaches items from their next move. When it no longer has a status some items are in, Workflow updates lists them: map that status to a step, then Take version n moves them there as one change.
features.roles: Manage project workflows (Project administrator)

features.title: Dashboards: the project's and the environment's progress
features.summary: Dashboards on the left rail shows the project's dashboards and the environment's. Project progress, Branches, Data completeness and Review and comments are there from the start; Environment overview counts every project you may open.
features.roles: Everyone who can view the project, and is in a dashboard's audience

features.title: Tiles: numbers, bars and the items behind them
features.summary: A tile counts or measures the rows of a source (objects, sheets, required values, value statuses, workflow items, tasks, documents, markups, findings, projects), grouped or not. Click a number or a bar to list its items and open one.
features.roles: As the dashboard

features.title: Change a dashboard
features.summary: Edit changes the name and the tiles: add one from the catalogue, remove one, Save. Each save is a version; Versions lists the last 20 and restores one.
features.roles: A project dashboard: Manage project dashboards (Lead engineer, Project administrator); the organization's: Manage organization dashboards

features.title: Who sees a dashboard
features.summary: Who sees it: everyone in the project, Lead engineers or Project administrators. Show in E1 Reviewer offers the dashboard on the iPad.
features.roles: As editing the dashboard

features.title: Every-project dashboards
features.summary: A dashboard the organization makes for every project shows in each project with that project's data. Copy to this project makes it the project's own; Reset to the organization's brings the shared one back.
features.roles: Making one: Manage organization dashboards; copying and resetting: Manage project dashboards

features.title: Present a dashboard
features.summary: Present hides the controls and enlarges the tiles for a meeting; Stop presenting brings them back.
features.roles: As the dashboard

features.title: Progress, weights and the plan
features.summary: Progress is the credit of the step each item has reached, weighted by a number of your choice (or 1). Each workflow step's credit can be changed for the project. The plan gives the percentage progress should have reached by each date; the S-curve draws progress against it.
features.roles: Manage project workflows (Project administrator)

features.title: Trends: S-curve, burn-up, cumulative flow
features.summary: E1 records the numbers of every trend tile once a day. A trend shows one number over days, a burn-up done against total, cumulative flow the items in each step per day, and the S-curve progress by week against the plan.
features.roles: As the dashboard; recording today's numbers by hand: Manage project dashboards

features.title: Statuses in branches, and the Branches dashboard
features.summary: A status changed in a branch and in main is a conflict that proposes the lower status; signatures given in a branch are void after a later change there; main-only steps; the branch criterion; the Branches dashboard and a dashboard computed in one branch.
features.roles: Everyone who works in branches; Lead engineers for workflows

features.title: The cause and effect matrix: interlocks, causes and effects
features.summary: On any unit or loop in Systems: add interlocks, the trips that start them and what they act on, see the matrix and the narrative E1 writes from them.
features.roles: Editor; a project role that may edit objects

features.title: Safety instrumented functions: required SIL, PFD and achieved SIL
features.summary: Make an interlock a safety instrumented function with its required SIL, give the failure rates and proof test interval, and see its PFD, achieved SIL and hardware fault tolerance.
features.roles: Editor; a project role that may edit objects

features.title: Alarms: priority, rationalization and plant states
features.summary: Add alarms on instruments, rationalize them so E1 proposes their priority, and see which alarms each plant state shows or suppresses.
features.roles: Editor; a project role that may edit objects

features.title: Plant states
features.summary: Name the states the plant runs in (Start-up, Normal operation, Shutdown, Maintenance): each alarm says in which of them it is suppressed.
features.roles: Editor; a project role that may change project settings

features.title: The cause and effect matrix and the alarm list as documents
features.summary: Make the matrix or the alarm list of a unit a document in Revisions, export it to Excel or PDF, and issue it like any document.
features.roles: Editor; a project role that may create documents

features.title: Open E1 Reviewer on the iPad and sign in
features.summary: Open your E1's /reviewer/ address in Safari on the iPad, sign in with your company account, and add it to the Home Screen; the E1 Reviewer app, once released, signs in the same way.
features.roles: Everyone with an E1 account

features.title: Your profile and organization
features.summary: The avatar in the top bar shows who is signed in, the organizations you belong to, the terms and conditions, and Sign out; tap another organization to work in it.
features.roles: Everyone

training.topic: Profile and organizations on the iPad

features.title: Terms and conditions on the iPad
features.summary: After you sign in for the first time, E1 Reviewer shows the E1 Terms and License Agreement; you accept it once for E1 and E1 Reviewer, and Profile → Terms and conditions shows it at any time.
features.roles: Everyone with an E1 account

features.title: The dashboard
features.summary: Home and each project's Overview show a dashboard of cards; in a project, every 2D space (with pins), the documents, pinned 2D spaces, redlines and recent changes.
features.roles: Everyone

features.title: Customize a dashboard for you, the project or the organization
features.summary: Customize adds, removes, orders and sizes the cards and saves the dashboard for you, for everyone in the project, or for everyone in the organization.
features.roles: Everyone for Just me; a project administrator for Everyone in the project; an organization administrator for Everyone in the organization

features.title: The Progress card: E1's dashboards on the iPad
features.summary: The Progress card shows E1's dashboards marked Show in E1 Reviewer, the environment's on Home and the project's in a project. Tap one to see it read-only; tap a number or a group to list its items and open one.
features.roles: Everyone; a tile counts only what you may open

features.title: Projects as tiles you arrange
features.summary: Home shows your projects as tiles; touch and hold a tile, or tap Arrange, and drag the tiles into the order you want. The order is kept for you.
features.roles: Everyone

features.title: A project's 2D spaces
features.summary: A project lists its 2D spaces on the left, and the list can be hidden; the 2D space shows as E1 draws it. One finger moves it, two fingers zoom; pin the 2D spaces you use most.
features.roles: Everyone with a role in the project

features.title: An object or a connection: properties, attributes, history and chat
features.summary: Tap a symbol, a pipe, a signal or a cable on a 2D space to see its object: properties, every attribute, its history and its chat.
features.roles: Everyone with a role in the project; writing in the chat needs a role that may comment

features.title: Photos and voice notes
features.summary: Take a photo with the iPad's camera or record a voice note and add it to an object, a comment or a task; they are kept with the object's files in E1.
features.roles: Everyone with a role in the project that may edit the object (adding files)

features.title: Redline a 2D space
features.summary: Redline draws on a 2D space with a pen, a cloud, an arrow, text or a stamp; each mark says what it means and carries a note, goes into a review round, and is answered by the engineers in E1.
features.roles: Everyone with a role in the project that may comment; setting another person's status needs a role that may resolve comments

features.title: For me: your tasks and checklists
features.summary: For me lists the tasks and checklists assigned to you in every project; tick the items, add items, comment with photos and voice notes, and mark a task done.
features.roles: Everyone; ticking needs the task to be yours or a role that may edit it

training.topic: Tasks and checklists on the iPad

features.title: Offline in a walk-down
features.summary: Without the connection, what was opened on the iPad stays readable, and redlines, comments, photos, voice notes and ticks wait to be sent.
features.roles: Everyone

features.title: Search
features.summary: The search field finds projects, 2D spaces, objects and connections by tag or name, and tasks; an object opens as its own page, with its 2D spaces one tap away.
features.roles: Everyone

features.title: Alex on the iPad
features.summary: Alex on the iPad is Ask: questions typed or spoken with the microphone, answered without changing anything.
features.roles: Everyone with a role in the project
